newsitem.title: USA: Lawyers plan probe, lawsuits on behalf of Jewell.
newsitem.headline: Lawyers plan probe, lawsuits on behalf of Jewell.

text.p: An attorney for former Olympic bomb suspect Richard Jewell said on Monday his legal team expected to bring lawsuits against NBC-TV, news anchor Tom Brokaw and the Atlanta Journal-Constitution newspaper for defamation.

Lin Wood also told a news conference he would investigate any involvement of the Atlanta Committee for the Olympic Games in news leaks that branded the former security guard as a suspect in the July 27 Olympic bombing.

Wood said he intended to investigate a "series of coincidences and facts" involving the timing of a news leak that implicated his client. The news that Jewell had been named a suspect in the investigation appeared in an issue of the Atlanta Journal-Constitution on the same day that Centennial Olympic Park reopened following the blast.

Wood contended that ACOG security chief Bill Rathburn at one point had authority over the FBI and Georgia state investigators. "The Atlanta Committee for the Olympic Games wanted a park that was deemed safe," Wood said. "They wanted the focus of the last week of the Olympic games taken away from the bombing."

He said he was not accusing ACOG of leaking any information about Jewell but he intended to find out what its role in the matter was. "I am telling you that I intend to look into whether they leaked this information," he said.

Jewell's lawyers previously said that they intended to sue several news organizations and continued to look at the possibility of a lawsuit against the federal government. Wood and his law partner, Wayne Grant, said they would pursue news outlets and reporters who not only cast Jewell as the suspect in the investigation but also implied he was the bomber.
